title.narrative: WLSA Swaziland Institutional Support and Capacity Building Project

description.narrative:
Over the last 3 years, CAFOD has supported WLSA-Swaziland to implement women and girls empowerment projects in Swaziland through DFID Match Funding and with financial support from the EU, through the European Instrument for Democracy and Human Rights (EIDHR). Through the support, WLSA-Swaziland developed a the first ever national women’s charter - a document which was developed through extensive consultations with women’s groups, and it presents Swazi women’s aspirations and demands on how they want their rights to be addressed; set up a community paralegal system – the paralegals comprise of community volunteers who were trained on basic human rights, and for the past three years they have been providing legal support and referral assistance to women and girls; and engaged with policy makers at community and national levels on women and girls’ rights – including equipping traditional leaders with knowledge on girls and women’s rights. In addition, CAFOD technical support has enabled WLSA to appoint a strong Board of trustees to give strategic direction to the organization and a vibrant staff compliment of qualified personnel who responsible for the day to day implementation of field programmes.
Despite the not-so-conducive funding environment (especially because Swaziland is classified as a lower middle income country hence do not attract many donors), a number of donors has registered some interest to invest in the work that WLSA-Swaziland is doing. For example, with a small grant from the National Endowment for Democracy (NED), WLSA is implementing an initiative which seeks to project women`s voices through active civic participation (project ends 30th September 2016), and with funding through the U.S. Ambassador’s community grants on adolescents, WLSA is implementing a community project with the aim of creating an enabling social and legal environment for adolescents in combating HIV/AIDS (project ends 30 November 2016). These are however small grant with little contribution towards institutional support.
WLSA-Swaziland has also sent out funding applications to OSISA, Magna Carta, Mama Cash and the Commonwealth. These are still being considered. CAFOD financial support will help WLSA-Swaziland to effectively implementing the small grants (which are building on the work that CAFOD has been supporting), and enable the partner to continue offering legal advice and assistance to indigent women and girls, raise awareness raising through media, conducting Parliamentary observation and make submissions on Bills and participate in cultural activities.
